messages:
jamie_infra: Heads-up — after pushing NVIDIA driver 550.16 to staging GPU nodes in eu-west-1, ~12/48 nodes failed to boot with DKMS build errors. Reverting the apt roll but I wanted to surface; could be a kernel-headers mismatch or a change in our build flags. :frowning:

gpubuild-bot: Auto-alert: 12 nodes failed DKMS build for nvidia/550.16 during postinstall. See logs at /var/log/gpu-builds/550-2026-03-17.tar.gz :rotating_light:

jamie_infra: Pasted tail of the build log from one affected host:```
/var/lib/dkms/nvidia/550.16/build/make.log
ERROR: Kernel configuration is invalid.  Try rebuilding your kernel and/or check the path to kernel source.
make[1]: *** [modules] Error 2
make: *** [all] Error 2
```

neha: Thanks for flagging. Do we have the host kernel version? My suspicion is that the kernel in staging is 6.1.16 but headers package installed is 6.1.15 (we hit that last month). Can you run `uname -r` and `ls /lib/modules/ | head`?

jamie_infra: On one node: `uname -r` -> `6.1.16-rt-rc1`
`ls /lib/modules/` -> `6.1.15-rt-rc1 5.15.102`
So headers missing for current running kernel.

matt_ops: That explains DKMS failing — it can't find matching headers to compile kernel modules. Two options: (1) install matching linux-headers package and re-run `dkms autoinstall`, or (2) roll back the kernel to 6.1.15 on those hosts so the already-installed headers match. For a quick mitigation we should pin driver back to 535 on staging.

ranjit_sre: Agreed on pinning drivers. Also note that our node provisioner occasionally boots into a newer kernel after a security apt upgrade; we need a pre-check in the driver rollout to ensure `linux-headers-$(uname -r)` is present. Adding to runbook.

jamie_infra: Rolling back in progress — apt installing `nvidia-driver-535=535.86.05-1` on affected nodes now. Staging capacity dropped to ~75% for ~30m.

deploy-bot: Rolling deployment paused by jamie_infra at 1754009980. Canary hosts excluded from further 550 rollout.

neha: Two additional notes: (a) some nodes show DKMS errors referencing `NVIDIA: running module version sanity check failed` — that's typically when kernel ABI changes and we need a full module rebuild; (b) check that /usr/src/nvidia-550.16 contains the expected patchset — our packaging added a new KBUILD flag in 550 that we didn't test against rt kernels.

jamie_infra: Found this snippet in `dkms status` on a broken host:```
nvidia, 550.16, 6.1.16-rt-rc1, x86_64: build failed
```
I tried `dkms autoinstall -m nvidia -v 550.16` and got the same make error. Installing `linux-headers-6.1.16-rt-rc1` fixed one host and `modprobe nvidia` succeeded.

matt_ops: Good. For the remaining nodes, if headers aren't available in our apt mirror, we should copy headers from a working host or rebuild initramfs? But copying is fragile. Long term: the driver rollout job should fail fast if `apt-cache policy linux-headers-$(uname -r)` shows no candidate.

ranjit_sre: Also keep an eye on NCCL and CUDA runtime compatibility — a partial driver downgrade can leave CUDA toolkit libs mismatched. I saw one container warn: `libnvidia-ml.so.1: version 'NVML_352' not found` during a smoke test. Run our embedding job smoke test after any driver change.

jamie_infra: Noted — I ran the smoke generator on the canary and got `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./smoke-test` -> OK on 535; on a host where I forced 550 with headers installed, we got a warning about `cuda driver API version mismatch` but the process completed.

neha: Action items: 1) Pin 535 across staging until we ensure headers are in place and packaging fixes KBUILD flags. 2) Add preflight header check to rollout pipeline. 3) Add smoke test gating (GPU health + NVML version check). I'll make the PR for the pipeline change.

matt_ops: I'll finish the rollback and schedule a follow-up to re-run 550 on a small rt-kernel matrix. Also want to add `--no-dkms` option in our packer jobs so we can deploy driver runfile as fallback if DKMS fails.

jamie_infra: Cost/impact note — rollback doubled our staging churn (reboots) and pushed some jobs to other regions; we saw ~6 hours of degraded capacity which will show up in the infra incident cost report. Keep finance in the loop if this extends.

ranjit_sre: We should also check dedicated pools — if customer Dedicated nodes get auto-updated headers and a driver rollout is attempted, that would be a critical outage. Add a protection to avoid driver upgrades on Dedicated pools unless explicitly approved.

deploy-bot: Follow-up checklist created: [ ] pin-staging-535, [ ] pipeline-preflight-headers-check, [ ] run-kernel-matrix-tests, [ ] dedicated-blocker-flag. Assigned to neha, matt_ops, jamie_infra, ranjit_sre.

jamie_infra: Closing the thread for now — will re-open if any staging host flips back to failed state. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:
